description: Contribution to Cold-Formed Steel Seismic Design within CFS-NHERI Project is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Joel Conte, University of California San Diego (ucsd.edu). This project uses Cold-Formed Steel (CFS) to address the need for multi-hazards resilient buildings. The research conducted was to correlate observed physical damage from video with key analog measurements at different performance levels. In addition, a 3D AutoCAD model complete with architecturally finishes of 10-story CFS test buildings was created. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-fq2w-5b71. Keywords: Cold-Formed Steel, ductility, durability, shear wall, gravity wall, tie-rod. Published 2021-09-29. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
